CAMR Personal gives a small model on your own computer a long-term memory. The model is used as downloaded and never retrained. What it learns is kept as notes beside it, and for each question it reads only the few notes that matter. This release makes its answers checkable: each short factual answer shows whether memory confirms it.

## Downloads

| Your computer | File |
|---|---|
| Windows (most PCs) | `camr-personal-windows-x64.zip` |
| Windows on ARM (Surface Pro X, Snapdragon laptops) | `camr-personal-windows-arm64.zip` |
| Mac with Apple chip (M1 or newer) | `camr-personal-macos-arm64.tar.gz` |
| Mac with Intel chip | `camr-personal-macos-x64.tar.gz` |
| Linux (x86-64) | `camr-personal-linux-x64.tar.gz` |
| Linux (ARM64) | `camr-personal-linux-arm64.tar.gz` |

**Get started**
1. Install [Ollama](https://ollama.com/download), open it, and pull a chat model: `ollama pull qwen2.5:1.5b`
2. Unzip the download and run `camr-personal`. Your browser opens at http://127.0.0.1:8502.
   - **Windows:** if SmartScreen warns, choose *More info → Run anyway* (the app is not code-signed yet).
   - **macOS:** the first time, right-click the file and choose *Open*, or run `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine camr-personal`.
3. On first run, click **Download memory model**. This fetches the search model (about 270 MB) through Ollama, once.

Everything stays in `~/.camr/` on your computer. The app only accepts requests from your own computer. Full guide: [docs/APP.md](https://github.com/Satasdin/CAMR/blob/v0.4.0/docs/APP.md).

## What's new since 0.2.1

**Answers you can trust**
- A fact memory already holds is answered straight from memory, without the model.
- Other short factual answers are checked against what memory read and labelled **Verified** (with the supporting line and its source), **Not confirmed**, or **Not checked**.
- **Strict mode** (*Only state facts memory confirms*): an answer memory does not confirm is shown only as a lead, marked unverified.
- Search combines meaning and exact words (hybrid search). On 196,000 notes it found the right note in the top 10 for 84.3% of questions, against 75.4% with meaning alone.

**It learns what it doesn't know**
- For a general question it has no notes on, it looks it up (DuckDuckGo, then Wikipedia), keeps what it read with the link, and answers from that. Next time it answers from memory, offline. A lookup that only finds a note about something else no longer stops the search.
- For a question about *you*, nothing is sent anywhere. It asks you to teach it (**✦ Teach me**).
- **◎ Learning** panel: what it looked up, how big its memory is next to the frozen model, and *knowledge packs* (ready-made memory you install in one click).
- **Sleep:** after 10 quiet minutes it tidies duplicate notes, looks up names it keeps seeing, and tries a better search setting. It keeps the change only if it helps.

**Fixes**
- Names at the start of a sentence ("Josh decides …") are no longer dropped when memory picks out who a note is about.
- The repository checks out on Windows again (cached file names contained `:`).

## Which model to pick

| Model size | Time for a short answer* | Memory used | Use it when |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.5B | 0.31 s | 0.66 GB | Very old or small computers |
| **1.5B (recommended)** | 0.52 s | 1.3 GB | Most laptops. Facts stop improving beyond this size. |
| 3B | 1.0 s | 2.8 GB | You ask questions that need two facts joined |
| 7B | 2.0 s | 4.8 GB | A fast computer and harder questions |

\*One short answer from one note, measured on a 4-core CPU with no graphics card.

## What the study found

The full results are in [FINDINGS.md](https://github.com/Satasdin/CAMR/blob/v0.4.0/docs/FINDINGS.md). The plain-language thesis chapter is in [docs/report/Chapter5_CAMR.pdf](https://github.com/Satasdin/CAMR/blob/claude/engine-build-docs-yfw9u0/docs/report/Chapter5_CAMR.pdf).

- **Model sizes.** 22 models were tested, from 0.5 to 14.8 billion parameters. With CAMR, every size from 1.5B up averaged 73–77% on facts about less-known subjects. Kimi K3, a large cloud model, scored 66.7% alone. Every model of 6B or more was slower than the cloud model.
- **Against today's standard (RAG).** Nine ways of giving a model documents were tested on the same 200 questions. With a small 0.5B model, CAMR got 62.5% right and 3.5% wrong; the best alternative got 45.5% right and 47.0% wrong. With the cloud model, the best alternative answered more (71.5% against 63.0%) but stated about five times as many wrong answers.
- **Business automations (n8n).**
  - Support desk: the cloud model with CAMR resolved 75% of tickets with no wrong replies, and handed every unanswerable ticket to a person.
  - Office agent: the cloud model went from 0% of tasks done to 100% with memory.
  - Daily news: the cloud model alone got 22% right; with CAMR it got 94%.
- **Cost.** The whole study used $33.36 of Kimi K3 API time for 6,456 calls.
- **Checks.** All 204 automated tests pass, and the one-command replay reproduced 16 of 16 results identically.

**Limits.** Memory does not fix reasoning: for maths a stronger model or a calculator is still needed. Lookups need an internet connection the first time.
